Martin — thanks for the questionnaire and the clear asks. Below are concise answers keyed to your sections; I’ve attached a short content risk matrix and our incident runbook for your review. If you’d like, we can follow up with a live 45‑minute vendor security walkthrough next week (I’ve included potential slots below).

1) Detection coverage & approach- Redwood combines model‑level safety filters, deterministic policy classifiers, and heuristic/semantic detectors that run on both requests and generated outputs. For banking‑sensitive classes (fraud scripts, PII exfiltration, social engineering prompts) we layer:
  • pretrained policy classifiers tuned to financial risk taxonomies
  • vector similarity against a customer‑provided corpus of known bad examples (configurable)
  • runtime anomaly scoring (unusual rate, sequence of requests, token patterns)

2) Signals for automated escalation- Alerts are triggered when a weighted score crosses thresholds. Signals include policy classifier confidence, embedding similarity > configurable T, abnormal request rate per API key, and cross‑session correlation. Escalation policies are configurable per customer and can:
  • open an incident in Redwood Console
  • send webhook/SN event to customer SIEM (Splunk/Datadog/QRadar)
  • trigger a hold on the model route (block further generations)

3) Telemetry & reporting- Customers receive token‑level traces, policy hit summaries, and anomaly timelines. Data available via:
  • Console dashboards and per‑route CSV exports
  • Webhooks/streaming events to your ingest pipeline
  • Audit logs (immutable, time‑ordered) that satisfy common regulatory controls

4) Customer controls (tuning & blocking)- Controls exposed via API/Console:
  • per‑route threshold sliders (sensitivity)
  • category suppression lists and allowlists
  • automatic fallback to safer model variants or deterministic response templates
  • ability to opt into human‑in‑the‑loop review queues for high‑risk prompts

5) Performance & accuracy measures- We publish per‑model policy classifier precision/recall on our verification corpus and share sample ROC curves under NDA. Typical financial‑risk classifier baseline (internal): precision 0.92 at recall 0.78 on a tuned fintech dataset; we will provide benchmark artifacts in our SOW (see attached matrix).

6) Incident runbook & SLAs- Attached (runbook_incident_report_template.docx). Highlights:
  • Incident creation and triage within 15 minutes for P1 policy breaches
  • Initial internal notification and customer webhook within 30 minutes
  • Post‑incident summary within 72 hours

7) Attestations / compliance- We can provide a SOC 2 summary and auditor contact under NDA; summary attached (soc2-summary-2026.pdf). Full SOC reports and penetration test artifacts are available under executed NDA and data access controls.
